decision.detail: I am already sitting in the chair behind the patch board, the one with the dip where I sat beside Alma an hour ago. My hands are flat on the desk. The reel is threaded. The regional line is lit green. I do not dial Pittsburgh. I do not press play. I do not route the tape. I lift my hands off the desk, let them drop to my thighs, and I sit in the booth for the rest of the evening. The projector in the next room is humming. I can feel it through the wall, a low mechanical pulse. I do not go to the ballroom. I do not open my notebook. I do not call Phil at the terminal. I do not call Larry. I sit. The green lamp on the line stays lit. The tape sits on the patch, threaded and ready, going nowhere tonight. I will send it tomorrow. Or I will not. That is a decision for a different evening. Tonight I am in the chair, and the machine is humming, and the dip in the seat is still warm from where Alma's hip was, and I am not a producer right now, I am a woman sitting in a booth in February, and that is the whole evening.
decision.intention: Be in the room where she was. Let the recording sit. Let the line stay open and unused. Let the evening be small and mine and not a deliverable. The tape will be there in the morning. Pittsburgh will wait one night. I will not package a dead woman's last words into a broadcast segment tonight. I will sit with the hum of the projector and the shape of the chair and the fact that she was here, forty-two winters, and I was beside her, and that is enough for one evening.
decision.words: Silence. I do not speak to the booth. I do not speak to the tape. I do not say her name. I breathe. The projector hums. I breathe again.
